subject.title: fix(browser): keep guarded CDP sockets on validated endpoints [AI]

question: Should explicit Chrome MCP `cdpUrl` profiles under restrictive Browser CDP policy fail closed until Chrome MCP can accept a policy-preserving pinned transport?
rationale: This is an intentional security-versus-compatibility policy choice: retaining the old subprocess attachment path would leave the validated destination unbound, while rejecting it can break existing guarded remote-CDP setups.

options.title: Accept the guarded fail-closed boundary
options.body: Keep the migration error for explicitly guarded Chrome MCP CDP URLs and direct affected users to the regular `openclaw` driver or host-local attachment.

options.title: Require a compatible pinned transport
options.body: Hold the behavior change until Chrome MCP can attach through a reviewed relay or transport that preserves the approved DNS destination.

options.title: Narrow the restriction
options.body: Keep the old attachment path only for a specifically approved policy mode with documented security and migration consequences.

recommendation.title: Accept the guarded fail-closed boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the migration error for explicitly guarded Chrome MCP CDP URLs and direct affected users to the regular `openclaw` driver or host-local attachment.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Browser CDP and session-hardening ownership is the strongest available signal for accepting the security and compatibility contract.
